author: Glenn Erby
title: Ranking Ravens' first-round picks by 2026 importance - NewsBreak
text:
By Glenn Erby ,
8 hours ago Nov 27, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton (14) reacts after stopping Cincinnati Bengals on fourth down during the first half at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images By Tommy Gilligan, Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images The Baltimore Ravens have one of the NFL's strongest groups of former first-round picks, with a mix of franchise pillars, defensive stars, young starters, and players facing pivotal seasons.
This ranking is not based strictly on career accomplishments. It is about the importance of the Ravens in 2026. That means positional value, role in the team's identity, contract status, roster dependency, replacement difficulty, and the consequences if the player does not perform all matter. Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, Trey Hendrickson, Chidobe Awuzi,e and several other key Ravens are not included because they were not first-round picks.
The list is limited to current Ravens who were selected in the first round of the NFL Draft.
1. Lamar Jackson, quarterback
Jackson is the clear No. 1 because everything the Ravens do starts with him. The two-time MVP is Baltimore's franchise quarterback, offensive engine, and most irreplaceable player. The Ravens can win in different ways, but their championship ceiling is tied directly to Jackson's health, efficiency, and ability to stress defenses with his arm and legs.
After an injury-plagued 2025 season, Jackson's sharp offseason work is one of the most important developments in Baltimore. The Ravens re-signed Tyler Huntley and released Cooper Rush, giving them a familiar backup, but there is no real replacement for what Jackson provides. Among current Ravens first-round picks, no one is more important.
2. Kyle Hamilton, safety
Hamilton is the most important defensive first-round pick on the roster because he changes the structure of Anthony Weaver's defense. His ability to play deep, cover tight ends, blitz, fit the run, and align near the line of scrimmage gives Baltimore one of the NFL's most versatile defensive weapons.
The Ravens lost Ar'Darius Washington and Alohi Gilman in free agency, then added Jaylinn Hawkins as a third safety. Malaki Starks gives the unit another first-round talent, but Hamilton remains the player who drives the secondary's flexibility. His value goes beyond traditional safety play, which is why he ranks this high.
3. Roquan Smith, linebacker
Smith remains one of Baltimore's most important players because he is the leader of the defense and the central figure at linebacker. He had another 100-tackle season and is under contract for two more years. Still, the long-term countdown has begun for Baltimore's eventual transition away from one of its most expensive defensive veterans.
For 2026, Smith is still essential. He communicates, corrects mistakes, controls the middle of the field, and gives the Ravens the physical identity they have long valued. Teddye Buchanan is coming off a torn ACL, Trenton Simpson is entering the final year of his rookie deal, and young linebackers such as Jay Higgins IV are still developing. Smith's importance is obvious.
4. Ronnie Stanley, left tackle
Stanley ranks this high because left tackle remains one of the hardest positions to replace. When healthy, he gives Baltimore reliable protection for Jackson's blind side and stability for an offense that still wants to control games with the run game and play-action concepts.
The Ravens have strong starting tackles with Stanley and Roger Rosengarten, but the depth behind them is thin. Carson Vinson and Gerad Lichtenhan are reserve options, which increases Stanley's importance. His health has been a storyline for years, but his role remains one of the most valuable on the roster.
5. Zay Flowers, wide receiver
Flowers is Baltimore's most important wide receiver and one of the most important first-round picks on the roster. The Ravens picked up his $27.3 million fifth-year option after back-to-back Pro Bowls, confirming his status as a core offensive piece around Jackson.
The Ravens added Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt to change the look of the receiver room, while Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, and LaJohntay Wester are also competing for roles. That depth helps, but Flowers remains the top target among wide receivers and the player most capable of creating separation, gaining yards after the catch, and making explosive plays.
6. Marlon Humphrey, cornerback
Humphrey remains one of Baltimore's most important defensive backs, even with a $26 million cap hit that creates financial discussion. The Ravens still expect him to have a prominent role, and his ability to play both outside and inside, as well as in matchup situations, makes him valuable in a conference loaded with elite quarterbacks.
Nate Wiggins, Chidobe Awuzie, T.J. Tampa, Chandler Rivers, and other corners give Baltimore depth, but Humphrey's experience and versatility remain important. His importance would rise even more if the Ravens lean on younger defensive backs in bigger roles.
7. Malaki Starks, safety
Starks ranks this highly because of his draft investment, role clarity, and how he fits alongside Hamilton. Baltimore used a first-round pick on him last year, and he enters 2026 as a projected starter in a secondary that should be one of the defense's strengths.
Hamilton is the established star, but Starks' development could determine how much flexibility Weaver has on the back end. If Starks becomes a dependable every-down safety, Baltimore can move Hamilton around freely and disguise coverages more aggressively. That makes Starks one of the most important young players on the roster.
8. Nate Wiggins, cornerback
Wiggins is entering his third season and remains a key piece of the Ravens' secondary. His importance is tied to his age, coverage traits, and Baltimore's need to keep developing affordable defensive backs behind veteran contracts.
Humphrey and Awuzie provide veteran presence, but Wiggins has the upside to become a long-term answer outside. In an AFC filled with high-level passing attacks, the Ravens need him to keep progressing. He is not as established as Humphrey, but his long-term importance is significant.
9. Vega Ioane, offensive guard
Ioane has not yet built an NFL résumé, but his immediate importance is high because Baltimore drafted him in the first round to become a Day 1 starter at guard. The Ravens are reshaping the interior offensive line after Tyler Linderbaum's departure, and Ioane is expected to be part of the solution.
Interior offensive line play matters even more with Jackson and Henry in the backfield. The Ravens need movement, power, and consistency up front, and Ioane's transition will be one of the biggest offensive storylines in camp. He ranks below the established stars because he has to prove it, but his role is important right away.
10. Rashod Bateman, wide receiver
Bateman is the first-round pick under the most pressure, but he is not the most important first-round pick on the roster because Baltimore has more options at wide receiver than it has had in recent years. Flowers is the clear top target, while Lane, Sarratt, Walker, and Wester give the Ravens new competition and roster flexibility.
That does not make Bateman unimportant. He is under contract through 2029, has the route-running ability to be a valuable outside receiver,r and still has a path to a major role. But his importance depends on whether he holds off younger receivers and turns talent into reliable weekly production. The Ravens would benefit if he becomes a trusted starter, but they are no longer built to wait on him by default.
Final ranking
Lamar Jackson Kyle Hamilton Roquan Smith Ronnie Stanley Zay Flowers Marlon Humphrey Malaki Starks Nate Wiggins Vega Ioane Rashod Bateman The Ravens' first-round importance ranking starts with the obvious: Jackson sets the ceiling for the entire franchise, while Hamilton and Smith drive the defense. Stanley's health remains central to the offensive structure, Flowers is the top wide receiver, and Humphrey is still one of Baltimore's most trusted defensive backs.
The most important developments beyond the stars will come from the young first-rounders. Starks and Wiggins can help shape the next version of Baltimore's secondary, while Ioane must become a quick answer on the interior offensive line. Bateman still has the talent to matter, but the depth around him means his importance now depends on whether he can re-establish himself in a reshaped receiver room.
Final analysis For a team with championship expectations, the Ravens do not need every former first-round pick to carry the roster. They need Jackson to stay healthy, Hamilton to remain elite, Smith to command the defense, Stanley to protect the blind side, and the younger first-rounders to grow quickly enough to keep Baltimore's roster among the AFC's best.
